ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
Humble supplication before the Divine: the speaker asks only to take the dust from the feet of the Saints and press it to their own forehead. The gesture is an act of surrender, reverence and self-abasement — placing oneself beneath the devout, seeking their grace as the one true treasure and the fulfilment of all spiritual attainments.

Themes: dust of the Saints, humility, surrender, reverence for the devout, grace, spiritual treasure, self-abasement
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
A humble plea for grace: the speaker asks the Divine to grant the dust of the Guru's Sikhs' feet, believing that even a sinner can attain spiritual liberation through contact with that sanctifying dust. The image of foot-dust is both an act of self-abasement and a claim that association with the devout transmits transformative power.

Themes: humility, grace, dust of the saints' feet, sangat (company of the devout), redemption of sinners, spiritual liberation, devotion, surrender
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
Bowing in reverence to the humble devotees and pressing the dust of their feet to one's face expresses utter self-abasement before the sangat (company of the devout). The speaker longs to join the saints in singing the Divine's praises, treating even the soil touched by their feet as sacred. The gesture declares that humility and service to the devoted are the path to union.

Themes: humility before the sangat, dust of the saints' feet, self-abasement, reverence for devotees, longing for holy company, surrender through service, sacredness of the humble
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
A plea for the privilege of humble service to the Lord’s devoted servant: waiting upon him and wiping his feet with one’s own hair. The gesture joins bodily self-offering with reverence for the holy, seeking closeness to God through menial care of those who belong to Him.
Themes: seva (selfless service), humility, devotion to the Lord’s servant, self-abasement, sacred labour, reverence for the holy, grace.
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
A plea framed as a single request: the speaker asks the Divine for the gift of the dust of the saints' feet, naming this as the only peace worth having. The image of dust expresses both humility and the desire to be close to those who live in the Divine presence; it is not a general wish for happiness but a specific longing for nearness to the holy, received as grace. The verse closes a passage with a personal petition.

Themes: grace as gift, the dust of the saints' feet, humility before the holy, yearning for nearness, refuge in the sangat, the peace that comes through surrender, divine blessing
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
A prayer of total self-offering before the saints: the speaker asks that his forehead rest at their feet, his eyes remain fixed on the sight of them, and his body be covered with the dust of their footsteps. The posture is one of humility, reverence, and longing for the transforming presence of the holy.

Themes: humility before the devout, longing for the sight of the holy, dust of the saints' feet, surrender, reverence, self-offering, spiritual aspiration
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
Praise of the Divine as supremely beautiful and captivating, the heart-enticer and Beloved who dwells within all beings yet remains utterly distinct and transcendent, immanent in creation but not confined by it. The refrain marks this as the central thought to pause on.

Themes: divine beauty, immanence and transcendence, beloved Lord, presence within all, distinctness from creation, praise, refrain
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
Ecstatic praise of the Divine's beauty in three aspects: naam (the divine Name), visible form, and the love or colour of devotion. The repetition of "beautiful" builds intensity, addressing the Divine as an intimate beloved. A refrain that anchors the composition in wonder and adoration rather than petition.

Themes: beauty of the divine Name, divine form, loving devotion, ecstatic praise, intimate address to the Divine, refrain, wonder, adoration
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
Praising the Divine as the embodiment of beauty and the fountainhead from which all sweetness, joy and spiritual flavour flow. Addresses the Beloved directly in the second person as the one source of every delight. ||1|| is a structural pause, not part of the meaning.

Themes: divine beauty, source of nectar, praise of the Divine, God as origin of joy, spiritual sweetness
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The speaker declares that the Divine is utterly pleasing to her eyes, and that the act of seeing the Beloved intoxicates and bewitches her. This is a love-struck confession of being captivated by the vision of the Divine presence, expressing the overwhelming attraction and ecstatic absorption that comes from direct spiritual sight.

Themes: divine beauty, spiritual intoxication, loving devotion, vision of the Beloved, ecstatic absorption, longing fulfilled, the captivating presence of the Divine
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The infinite, boundless glory of the merciful, beloved Lord of the universe is praised as supremely beautiful. The line exalts divine splendour, declaring that the compassionate Gopal's majesty has no limit and spreads everywhere.

Themes: divine glory, infinite beauty, mercy, praise of the Lord, boundless majesty, compassion
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine personally safeguards the honour of devotees in every place and is the one who enables them to practise simran (loving remembrance) of the divine Name. Preservation and devotion are both gifts, not human achievements; the servant is kept and made to remember by the same grace.

Themes: divine protection, grace as sole agency, naam, simran, preservation of honour, surrender, divine initiative
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Divine personally safeguards the honour of devotees, and this protection is not a one-time act but an unbroken pattern repeated in every age. A declaration of trust in the Lord's enduring commitment to those who surrender to Him, affirming that divine guardianship of the humble is the consistent, eternal order of history.

Themes: divine protection, honour of devotees, trust in the Lord, continuity across ages, surrender, divine faithfulness, refuge
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
Devotional address declaring a mutual bond of love: the Divine is the master of every devotee's life-breath and the beloved of their heart, while all devotees are dear to the Divine in return. The image is intimate and reciprocal — not distant worship but a living relationship in which the Divine cherishes the worshipper as much as the worshipper longs for the Divine.

Themes: mutual love between the Divine and devotees, the Divine as life-master, reciprocal devotion, beloved Lord, intimate relationship with the Divine, divine affection for worshippers
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
The Divine is addressed directly as the sole support of devotees and the only refuge of the saints, affirming that the Creator is eternal and true. This is a declaration of dependence and trust, placing all security in the Divine rather than in any worldly power. The line functions as a refrain, anchoring the composition in the conviction that the Creator alone upholds those who love Him.

Themes: divine support, refuge in God, dependence on the Creator, protection of the saints, trust, eternal Creator, naam as shelter
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ: The Lord King creates His bhagats (devotees) in every age and has always come to preserve their honor when they face hardship. This is a declaration of divine faithfulness, assuring that the Sovereign personally safeguards the dignity of the faithful across time. Themes: divine protection, honor of devotees, creation of bhagats, sovereignty of God, deliverance in distress, recurring ages.
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
A plea for mercy that asks the Divine to set aside the record of one's deeds and instead act from the master's own obligation to protect a servant's honour. The devotee admits unworthiness yet appeals to the Lord's reputation, making preservation of the servant's dignity the Divine's own concern.

Themes: karma not weighed, appeal for grace, servant's honour preserved, divine responsibility, mercy over justice, refuge in the master
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
A humble supplicant asks daily for the divine Name, and the Sovereign Lord accepts the request. The stance is one of confident promise: persistent, lowly asking for naam (the divine Name) is never refused. Begging here is not humiliation but the proper posture of the soul before its Master, and the granting is certain.

Themes: persistent supplication, humility before the Divine, the divine Name as gift, prayer answered, grace, reliance on the Lord, spiritual poverty
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
A supplication asking for the gift of the divine Name (naam) as the sole cure for inner restlessness. The mind's craving is pictured as physical hunger that only contentment can end; receiving naam is what produces that contentment. The stance is petitionary, linking divine grace to the quenching of desire.

Themes: prayer for naam, contentment as antidote to craving, hunger of the mind, quenching desire, divine grace, inner peace, supplication
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
A soul stands before the Divine as a beggar, asking for nothing worldly but only the gift of naam (the divine Name), repeating the plea without end. The stance is one of humble supplication and single-pointed longing, declaring that the only true need is union with the Divine through the Name.

Themes: begging for the divine Name, humble supplication, longing for union, naam as the sole need, renunciation of worldly asking, persistent prayer, dependence on the Divine
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
A plea for enabling grace: the supplicant asks the merciful Lord, addressed as Gopal (nourisher of the world) and Gobind (lord of the universe), to grant the capacity to repeat the divine Name. Chanting is not presented as a human achievement but as a gift that must be bestowed. The pause marks this as the central refrain of the composition.

Themes: supplication, divine grace, naam (the divine Name), dependence on God, prayer as gift, loving repetition, humility
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
A humble supplicant begs for the gift of the divine Word, asking the Beloved to bestow it. The stance is one of utter dependence and longing, framing the devotee as a beggar before the Divine and the sought boon as charity only grace can give.

Themes: supplication, begging for divine grace, the devotee as beggar, longing for the Word, dependence on the Beloved, charity of the divine Name
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
A beggar at the Divine Door pleads for alms, asking not for worldly goods but for grace itself. The stance is humble supplication: the speaker owns his poverty and dependence, and the only gift worth begging for is the Lord's merciful glance. The image of the door makes the Divine a giver who can be approached, while the beggar's posture declares that everything received is unearned charity.

Themes: supplication, humility, divine grace, dependence on God, begging at the door, unearned gift, mercy, spiritual poverty
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
A single drop of the divine Name received into the soul makes the mind blossom and the body flourish with spiritual vitality, like parched ground turning green after rain. The image of one drop reviving the whole being declares that even minimal contact with naam (the divine Name) transforms a person entirely.

Themes: spiritual renewal, transformative power of naam, inner blossoming, vitality from divine grace, small effort yielding total change, flourishing of mind and body
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
Drinking the Lord's essence — the naam (divine Name) as amrit, immortal nectar — leaves a person permanently dyed in that colour. The image is of intoxication and saturation: one who tastes this inner rasa is never sober of it again, but lives continually steeped in loving absorption. It describes the abiding state that follows genuine inner experience of the Divine.

Themes: divine nectar, naam, permanent devotion, spiritual intoxication, inner saturation, loving absorption, transformed state
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
Singing the Lord's kirtan is itself the ambrosial essence that nourishes the soul; this is the only song worth singing. For one who does so, the unstruck celestial sound-current vibrates unceasingly within, day and night, as an inner music of spiritual bliss. The line is a central refrain, establishing the practice and its promised inner result.

Themes: kirtan as spiritual nourishment, divine praise, ambrosial nectar, inner sound-current, naad, continuous remembrance, day and night devotion, spiritual bliss
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
The tongue is addressed as a beloved companion and urged to drink the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name), the essence that grants spiritual life. The instruction frames sensory experience as a channel for devotion: taste itself is redirected from worldly pleasures toward the intoxicating sweetness of remembrance.

Themes: naam as nectar, spiritual sustenance, devotion through the senses, loving address to one's own body, redirecting desire, divine sweetness
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
The devotee is drunk on the essence of the divine Name, absorbed in an intoxication that comes not from wine but from loving remembrance of the Divine. The image of being overcome by a sublime elixir conveys total immersion, a state where the mind is saturated with the Divine presence and freed from ordinary awareness.

Themes: divine intoxication, naam (the divine Name), loving absorption, spiritual ecstasy, devotion, inner saturation, transcendence of worldly consciousness
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
Drinking the ambrosial essence of naam (the divine Name) through the Guru's shabad, the speaker declares total loving surrender — offering himself as a sacrifice to the Name. The line is a testimony of inner fulfilment: the Guru's word is the vessel through which the nectar of spiritual life is tasted, and that taste makes self-offering the only fitting response.

Themes: naam as nectar, drinking divine essence, Guru's shabad as means, self-sacrifice, loving surrender, spiritual intoxication, devotion as offering
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
The divine Name is praised as the highest, most life-giving essence, and the speaker asks how this ambrosial taste can be obtained and consumed. The line both exalts naam (the divine Name) and poses a searching question about the method of receiving it.

Themes: naam as supreme nectar, longing for spiritual taste, how to attain divine essence, seeking the method, praise of the Name, spiritual hunger
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
An exhortation addressed to fellow seekers: take in the divine essence as one would drink, fully and inwardly. The image of drinking the Lord's rasa (nectar, essence) frames naam (the divine Name) as something to be tasted and absorbed, not merely recited. The teeka grounds this in taking refuge with the perfect Guru and practising simran (loving remembrance). The line urges direct, experiential communion rather than distant worship.

Themes: drinking divine nectar, naam as rasa, exhortation to fellow seekers, refuge in the Guru, simran, inward absorption, divine sweetness, spiritual sustenance
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
Urges a female companion to abandon the insipid water of vice and sensual corruption, and instead drink the supreme nectar of naam (the divine Name). The contrast between tasteless poison and sweet amrit frames renunciation not as loss but as exchange for true flavour. It is affectionate exhortation, calling the soul to turn from maya (worldly attachment) toward lasting spiritual sweetness.

Themes: renunciation of vice, naam as nectar, spiritual sweetness, turning from maya, exhortation to the soul, divine taste, companionship in devotion
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
The pain of separation from the Divine is likened to a venomous serpent coiled inside the mind, so consuming that no spell or incantation can subdue it. The image declares that true longing for the Beloved, once awakened through surrender to the Guru, cannot be charmed away or silenced by any external remedy.

Themes: viraha (pang of separation), divine longing, inner serpent, incurable love, surrender to Guru, powerlessness of ritual remedies, consuming devotion
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
A desperate, intimate cry to the mother: life itself becomes unbearable without the Divine presence. The soul is restless and anguished apart from the Beloved, expressing utter dependence on the divine Name as the only sustainer of life.

Themes: separation from the Divine, longing, anguish, dependence on naam, soul's distress, intimate plea, life without God
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
A longing to meet the Divine has awakened in the mind, described as love directed toward union with the Beloved. The line declares an inner transformation: desire for God's presence is no longer external but has taken root in the heart. It frames spiritual yearning as the precondition for meeting the Divine.

Themes: longing for union with the Divine, love for the Beloved, inner awakening, devotional desire, the heart turned toward God, spiritual yearning as grace
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
Intense longing for the divine vision, compared to a thirsty person desperate for water. The mind burns and craves the sight of the Divine as a bodily need, not a mild wish. The speaker confesses the depth of this yearning to a companion, making desire itself the proof of love's wound.

Themes: longing for divine vision, thirst as spiritual metaphor, separation and yearning, intensity of devotion, confession of inner state, love's wound
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
The soul, pictured as a woman abandoned in a wilderness, laments that no one except the Beloved Divine Husband asks after her welfare; alone in the world-jungle she cries out. The line voices the anguish of separation from God and the utter insufficiency of all other relationships, declaring that only the Divine truly cares.

Themes: longing for the Divine, separation and anguish, soul as bride, wilderness of the world, helplessness without God, exclusive reliance on the Beloved, cry of the lonely soul
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
The mind has turned away from worldly entanglements and now burns with a single longing: to behold the Divine presence directly. This is a description of the inner state of a fortunate soul, where detachment from maya (worldly attachment) is not empty renunciation but the birth of love, and that love expresses itself as an ache to see the Beloved. The line declares that true yearning for the Divine vision arises only when the heart has first been emptied of the world.

Themes: inner detachment, longing for divine vision, darshan, love for the Divine, renunciation of maya, spiritual yearning, the fortunate soul
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
A longing plea addressed to the Divine as husband and beloved: return to the heart's home after long separation, and let union happen through the Guru's shabad (divine word). The soul asks not for a distant vision but for indwelling presence, merging with the Lord through sacred instruction.

Themes: longing for union, the Divine as beloved, return to the heart, separation and reunion, the Guru's shabad as meeting-place, indwelling presence, bridal soul, prayer of yearning
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The speaker absolves the Divine Husband, the giver of all peace, of any blame for her separation and instead indicts herself as the wrongdoer whose own evil actions caused the rift. It is a confession of personal responsibility, spoken in the voice of a soul-bride estranged from her Lord.

Themes: self-blame, separation from the Divine, divine innocence, personal wrongdoing, soul-bride, accountability, confession
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
An invitation addressed to the Guru, pleading for the divine presence to enter and dwell within the heart so that the ears may receive the Lord's praises. The longing is for direct, embodied hearing of sacred praise as the means of inner transformation, with the heart framed as a home prepared for the beloved guest.

Themes: longing for the Guru's presence, the heart as dwelling-place, hearing divine praise, inner receptivity, devotion as hospitality, the ear as gateway to the sacred
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
An intimate, urgent plea for the Beloved Lord to enter and abide within the heart. The voice is personal longing, not distant worship, inviting divine presence to make the heart its home. The beloved as inner guest, the heart as sacred dwelling-place, and the soul’s yearning for closeness all express one desire for union with the Divine.

Themes: divine intimacy, loving invocation, indwelling presence, yearning for the Beloved, heart as sacred dwelling, personal relationship with the Divine, supplication
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
A soul-bride's direct plea for the Divine Husband to show mercy and come dwell within her heart as its true home. The longing is for intimate, indwelling presence, not distant favor. The request frames the heart as the house awaiting its rightful master, and mercy as the act that brings the Beloved back inside.

Themes: heartfelt supplication, divine mercy, longing for union, the heart as home, soul-bride and Divine Husband, indwelling presence, return to the inner self
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
A soul-bride pleads with the Beloved to enter the house of her heart and dwell there. The entreaty is intimate and urgent, casting the Divine as an enchanting, fascinating presence whose arrival transforms the inner home. It is a prayer of longing, not a statement of attainment.

Themes: longing for divine presence, heart as dwelling-place, intimate prayer, soul-bride and Beloved, yearning, inner home, supplication
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The devotee celebrates that the Divine, as the beloved friend, has arrived and manifested within the heart-home. The line expresses joyful wonder at an intimate spiritual visitation, declaring the inner self now filled with the presence of the Beloved.

Themes: divine arrival, heart as home, inner presence, beloved friend, spiritual union, joy, manifestation
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥: Worship in the first watch of the night is like a tender flower, while the fruit comes only from devotion in the ambrosial hours before dawn. The image of flower and fruit teaches that early spiritual effort is beautiful but incomplete; mature attainment ripens through discipline sustained into the later watches. Themes: stages of spiritual growth, night vigil, ambrosial hours, patience in devotion, fruit of worship, progression from effort to attainment
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
Admonishing one's own soul for wasting life asleep in maya (worldly attachment). The sleep is not physical but spiritual unconsciousness, and the command is to wake from it and practice simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine. A sharp self-rebuke demanding urgency in devotion instead of drifting through existence.

Themes: spiritual lethargy, maya as sleep, urgency of devotion, simran, self-admonition, wasted life, awakening
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
An instruction for the ambrosial hours before dawn: rise and repeat the divine Name, fixing the mind on the Guru's feet as the humble, reverent gateway into that remembrance. The early morning is set apart as the time for this discipline, and the Guru's feet are both an object of meditation and the attitude of lowly devotion through which naam (the divine Name) takes root in the heart.

Themes: amrit vela, early morning discipline, naam japna, simran, reverence for the Guru, humility, meditation on the Guru's feet, daily spiritual practice
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
Rise in the ambrosial hour (amrit vela) and repeat the divine Name; let that worship continue unbroken through night and day. The instruction urges a dawn discipline that matures into constant inward remembrance, not a ritual confined to morning. Early rising becomes the gateway to naam (the divine Name), and every hour turns into continuous adoration.

Themes: amrit vela, early morning discipline, divine Name, continuous remembrance, night-and-day worship, loving devotion, spiritual routine
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ: The rainbird's cry in the ambrosial pre-dawn hour is an image of the soul's longing prayer offered at the spiritually potent time before dawn; such a call of yearning reaches the Divine court and is heard. It teaches that sincere supplication at the right moment gains divine attention. Themes: pre-dawn devotion, amrit vela, longing for the Divine, prayer heard, divine court, soul's cry, yearning, supplication answered
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing the praises of the Lord of the Universe brings a tangible physical and mental transformation: the chest becomes cool and calm, the mind rests in contentment. The act of devotional song is presented as the direct cause of inner peace, not merely an accompaniment to it.

Themes: cooling of the heart, inner peace through praise, devotional singing, Gobind's glory, mind at rest, transformative power of kirtan
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing the Divine praises is itself the attainment of true Yoga, the state of union and detachment that yogis strive for through arduous practices. Kirtan, the sung praise of the Divine, replaces ascetic discipline as the path to liberation, yielding both worldly contentment and the freedom of renunciation within the act of devotion.

Themes: kirtan as yoga, singing divine praise, union through devotion, effortless spiritual attainment, praise as spiritual practice, renunciation through song
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
An unbroken personal commitment: day and night the speaker sings kirtan (devotional singing), the praises of the divine Name (naam). The concrete act of singing is also the soul's ceaseless loving remembrance; every moment becomes worship, leaving no gap between adoration and living.  
Themes: ceaseless devotion, kirtan (devotional singing), naam (divine Name), praise of the Divine, unbroken remembrance, worship as constant activity, loving surrender.
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
Rise before dawn and join the sangat (company of the devout) to sing the Shabad, described as the unstruck, self-resounding melody that plays without any instrument. The instruction is devotional practice: daily, disciplined, collective singing of divine praise as the way to attune oneself to the ever-present sound current of the Divine.

Themes: early morning devotion, sangat, singing divine praise, unstruck sound, Shabad, daily spiritual discipline, collective worship
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
An exhortation addressed to the holy ones, urging them to continually sing the praises of Govind, the Lord of the Universe. It frames ceaseless devotional singing as the proper activity of the devout, directing the community toward perpetual glorification of the Divine rather than occasional worship.

Themes: divine praise, kirtan, exhortation to the devout, Govind, continual worship, glorifying the Divine, holy company
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
Singing the Creator's praises from a state of nirvaana — freedom from craving and mental impressions — is enjoined as the practice that liberates. Even a single instant of simran (loving remembrance of the divine Name) severs bondage to vice and worldly attachment. The emphasis is on the disproportionate saving power of brief, desireless remembrance expressed through kirtan.

Themes: nirvaana, freedom from desire, kirtan as praise of the Creator, simran, instantaneous liberation, release from vice, power of brief remembrance, devotional singing
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The mind accepts whatever the Divine ordains as sweet, without complaint or resentment. This is a declaration of surrendered contentment: no blame is ever laid on another for any excess or hardship, because all that comes is received as the Beloved's doing. The refrain marks this trusting acceptance as the core attitude being taught.

Themes: surrender to divine will, accepting hardship as sweetness, freedom from blame and complaint, contentment of mind, trust in the Beloved's decree, equanimity
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
The devotee declares that everything the divine Friend does feels like comfort and ease, not hardship. Whatever comes from the Beloved is received as sweet, welcome, and wholly good. This is a statement of loving trust and acceptance of the divine will.

Themes: divine will, acceptance, trust in the Beloved, sweetness of God's actions, loving surrender, contentment with what comes
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Accepting the divine will as sweet brings every form of peace, bliss, festivity and delight. The state is one of total contentment: not that pleasures arrive, but that whatever comes is experienced as pleasure because it is received as the Lord's command. A declaration of the fruit of surrender, placed as the refrain.

Themes: surrender to divine will, inner peace, bliss, contentment, acceptance, joy as response, divine decree
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The Divine creates and destroys in a single instant, holding every decision and outcome in His own hands. A declaration of absolute sovereignty: nothing arises or falls away outside His will, and human calculation has no final say. The image of the hand conveys direct, personal control over all affairs.

Themes: divine omnipotence, creation and destruction, sovereignty of the Divine will, impermanence, surrender of human agency, divine control over destiny
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
Meditating on the divine Name is presented as the practical solution to life's difficulties: when the mind is fixed in loving remembrance of God, every undertaking reaches successful completion. The line instructs and reassures, promising that spiritual focus resolves worldly affairs.

Themes: naam (divine Name), meditation, success in worldly affairs, divine remembrance, practical spirituality, resolution of difficulties
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
The mind is instructed that its worldly purpose will reach completion only through constant singing of the Divine praises. Repetition of "Har, Har, Har" is both the method and the assurance: devotion is not a distraction from one's affairs but the very means by which they succeed. A promise attached to an imperative.

Themes: divine praise as means to success, assurance of fulfillment, instruction to the mind, naam simran (loving remembrance), repetition of the Divine Name, devotion resolving worldly affairs
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Devotion to naam (the divine Name) is presented as the one practice that makes every human undertaking succeed. The line instructs rather than describes: make loving remembrance of the Divine your work, and life's purpose completes itself. Success is reframed not as worldly gain but as the fulfilment that comes through simran (loving remembrance).

Themes: naam, simran, remembrance of the Divine, life's purpose fulfilled, spiritual practice, success through devotion, instruction
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
All affairs are set right only when it pleases the Divine. The line declares that human effort is not what resolves life's difficulties; success comes solely through alignment with the divine will. It is a statement of surrender and trust, placing the outcome of every undertaking in the hands of the Beloved rather than in one's own striving.

Themes: divine will, surrender, grace, resolution of affairs, trust in the Divine, acceptance, providence
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
Declares the complete fulfillment that follows union with the Divine: every longing and desire reaches its end, and sorrow is permanently abolished. The state is one of total contentment, where lack and grief no longer exist. It presents this as the assured outcome of devotion, a promise of lasting peace rather than a temporary relief.

Themes: fulfillment of desires, end of sorrow, lasting contentment, divine union, freedom from suffering, spiritual completion
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The lotus feet of the Divine are the sole foundation and refuge for the humble servant. This declares total dependence on the Divine presence, presenting surrender at the feet as the only stable ground and shelter in life.

Themes: lotus feet, divine support, refuge, surrender, humble servant, dependence on God, anchor of life
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
Inward devotion to the lotus feet of the Divine, sustained by reliance on the perfect Guru. The speaker asks for grace to fix this contemplation within the heart, making the Guru the foundation of inner practice. It is a prayer for steadfast remembrance rather than a description of an achieved state.

Themes: lotus feet as divine presence, refuge and surrender, inner meditation, grace, reliance on the Guru, steadfast devotion, heart-centred worship
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
Loving the Lord's lotus feet — the divine presence as the ground of refuge and surrender — is a way of life that dwells only in the minds of the saints. The line declares that this love is not an occasional act but an established inner disposition, a settled practice of devotion that distinguishes the holy from the worldly.

Themes: lotus feet as divine refuge, love for the Divine, saintly disposition, inner devotion, way of life, surrender, divine presence
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
The mind is urged to board the boat of the Divine's lotus feet as the sole vessel for crossing the world-ocean. The lotus feet are both a concrete image of refuge at the Divine's presence and the means of passage beyond suffering and rebirth. The stance is direct instruction to one's own mind: embark now, for this alone carries one across.

Themes: lotus feet as vessel, crossing the world-ocean, refuge in the Divine, instruction to the mind, liberation, surrender, divine grace as crossing
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
The mind is transfixed, pierced through by the Lord's lotus feet — an image of tender refuge at the Divine presence — so that nothing else in existence tastes sweet anymore. This is a declaration of single-pointed devotion: once the heart is penetrated by loving absorption in the Divine, every other pleasure or attachment loses its flavour. The Lord alone, the sovereign King, remains desirable.

Themes: lotus feet as refuge, mind pierced by devotion, exclusive love for the Divine, sweetness only in God, detachment from other pleasures, single-pointed remembrance, surrender
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Drinking the amrit (divine nectar) of naam through the Guru's grace brings complete inner satisfaction, and the Guru grants a state beyond death and decay. The teeka explains this as an enduring spiritual elevation: old age, death, and suffering can no longer touch such a person. The line declares the transformative result of receiving the Guru's teaching—liberation from mortality and pain.

Themes: amrit, divine nectar, immortality, Guru's grace, spiritual satisfaction, liberation from death, freedom from suffering, naam
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Drinking the naam-ras (essence of the divine Name) produces spiritual intoxication; those who imbibe it become mast (enraptured, absorbed), and the entangling snares and bonds of maya (worldly attachment) snap apart. Describes the liberating effect of inner absorption, contrasting worldly captivity with the freedom that follows true inner drinking.

Themes: naam-ras, spiritual intoxication, liberation from maya, cutting of bonds, enraptured absorption, freedom from attachment
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
The mind is addressed directly: only the one who drinks the Lord's amrit—the nectar of naam that gives spiritual life—truly lives. Tasting this ambrosial water is an inner experience of the Divine presence, not a physical act. The line holds up the one who partakes as the model for the mind to follow, urging it toward that same nourishment.

Themes: naam as nectar, spiritual sustenance, inner experience of the Divine, admonishing one's own mind, true life, drinking amrit
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Guru has poured the life-giving nectar of the divine Name into the mouth, reviving a soul that was spiritually dead. This is a testimony of rescue: the Guru's grace reverses death and restores life. The image is of water poured into a parched mouth, and beneath it, the awakening that comes when naam (the divine Name) is received.

Themes: Guru's grace, spiritual resurrection, naam as nectar, death of the soul, revival, divine gift, transformation
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The divine Name is a treasure of amrit, the nectar that grants immortality, and the instruction is to gather in sangat, the company of the devout, and drink it together. The line exhorts seekers to share in the life-giving essence of naam rather than hoard it alone, presenting collective remembrance as the way to access the inexhaustible spiritual wealth.

Themes: amrit as immortalising nectar, naam as treasure, sangat and collective worship, drinking divine essence, shared spiritual practice, immortality through the Name
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The cycle of birth and death no longer holds any terror, and the soul is freed from returning to the womb. Liberation from transmigration is declared as an accomplished fact, not a hope: the fear that drives all human anxiety is cut away, and the round of rebirth ends entirely.

Themes: freedom from reincarnation, end of the birth-death cycle, fearlessness, liberation, divine grace, release from worldly suffering
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Attaining sahaj (intuitive poise, inner stillness), one finds the Divine, and with that finding the terror of death's messenger dissolves. The line declares a causal chain: mental equipoise leads to divine union, which removes existential fear. It describes the state of liberation as the natural result of inner calm.

Themes: sahaj, inner stillness, finding the Divine, fearlessness, liberation from death, spiritual attainment, peace
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
The fear that grips a person across birth, death, and the whole span of life is cut away through repeating the Word spoken by the humble servant of the Divine. This is a declaration of remedy: meditating on the servant's revealed utterance, especially within sangat (the company of the devout), severs the dread of mortality and the cycle of rebirth.

Themes: fear of birth and death, liberation from the cycle of rebirth, power of the divine Word, meditation and repetition, refuge in the humble servant, sangat, removal of existential dread
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine removes the terror of the whole human cycle — birth, aging, death and the anxieties that accompany them. The line is a promise and a reassurance: meditation on the divine Name is the remedy that frees the mind from existential dread, so that mortality no longer wounds.

Themes: simran, freedom from fear, birth and death, aging, mortality, divine remembrance, liberation from anxiety, the human condition
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
The cycle of birth and death is a wound that the sangat (company of the devout) alone can cut away; with it goes the dread of the Messenger of Death, who no longer holds any claim or threat over the liberated soul. The line promises release from existential suffering and from the terror of mortality as the direct result of spiritual fellowship.

Themes: end of reincarnation, freedom from fear of death, sangat, liberation, release from suffering, mortality, spiritual community
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
Freedom from the terror of reincarnation's endless cycle is declared as an accomplished fact. The fear that drives human anxiety — being born again and again only to die — has been entirely removed. This is a statement of liberation attained, not a hope or request, marking the inner state of one who has reached spiritual certainty. The bondage of repeated existence no longer holds sway.

Themes: liberation from rebirth, end of existential fear, spiritual freedom, cycle of birth and death, inner peace, release from transmigration, attained salvation
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Relying on the shelter of the Saadh Sangat, the company of the holy, a person becomes dyed in love for the Divine. The sangat is the enabling ground, the support that makes attachment to God possible; without it the heart remains unstained. Falling in love with God is presented not as solitary effort but as a gift received through holy association.

Themes: sangat as refuge, divine love, spiritual support, transformation through holy company, devotion kindled in community, reliance on the devout
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
The sangat (company of the devout) is presented as the vessel that carries a person across the world-ocean, and that same fellowship severs the noose of death. It is a declaration of the saving power of holy company: liberation from the cycle of fear and mortality is not achieved alone but through collective devotion.

Themes: sangat, world-ocean, liberation, death, salvation, holy company, crossing, divine rescue
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Joining the Saadh Sangat, the company of the holy, is the decisive event: once that fellowship is found, union with the Divine is accomplished. The utterance is a first-person witness that such company is not mere preparation but the very place where meeting the Lord happens. Fellowship with the devout grants immediate spiritual union, not delayed reward.  
Themes: Saadh Sangat, company of the holy, divine union, meeting the Lord, transformative fellowship, spiritual attainment, communal grace
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
The saints remain continually absorbed in the sangat (company of the devout), dyed in the beautiful, deep colour of divine love, and from that immersion they sing the praises of the Divine. The line describes a state of being: true devotion is not solitary but sustained through holy company, and praise flows naturally from hearts already coloured by love.

Themes: sangat, divine love, singing praise, spiritual immersion, devotion, holy company, transformation, worship
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
A plea for divine rescue: God is asked to pull the mind out of vice and corruption and fix it in the sangat, the company of the devout. The image is of extraction from a trap — being lifted out of maya (worldly attachment) and placed where the mind can hold to naam (the divine Name). The stance is supplication, asking for both removal and reattachment.

Themes: deliverance from vice, rescue from maya, longing for holy company, sangat as anchor, mind fixed on the divine, supplication, transformation through association
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
An intimate address urging friends to hear and absorb the greatness of the sadh sangat, the company of the devout. The speaker presents this fellowship as something worthy of praise and attention, framing it as a gift to be received through listening. The tone is warm, personal, and invitational, calling the listener into reverence for spiritual community.

Themes: praise of holy company, attentive listening, spiritual friendship, greatness of the devout, invitation to reverence, communal devotion
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
The Guru is declared identical with the Transcendent Lord, the supreme source of all comfort and peace. This is a personal testimony of trust, identifying the spiritual guide as the divine presence itself, the one who grants lasting ease and removes suffering.

Themes: Guru as divine form, source of peace, trust in the Guru, God as giver of comfort, spiritual refuge, personal declaration of faith
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
Direct address to the Divine, declaring that God alone is the Giver of all gifts and the Architect of destiny. The line praises divine sovereignty: every provision comes from God, and every fate is authored by God. It is an affirmation of total dependence, placing the source of both sustenance and life's unfolding entirely in divine hands.

Themes: divine sovereignty, God as giver, destiny, providence, dependence on God, praise, divine authorship, sustenance
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
A direct plea to the merciful Divine, addressed as the embodiment of kindness and the treasure-house of grace. Nanak asks for the blessed vision of the Divine presence, declaring that this darshan alone grants the state of redeemed, elevated spiritual life while still alive.

Themes: compassion, divine grace, supplication, darshan, spiritual liberation, jivan mukti, divine vision, mercy
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Direct address to the Divine as supreme sovereign, declaring God to be the great Lord and Master who is filled with all virtues and of profound, unfathomable depth. The line is an act of praise and recognition, affirming divine majesty, moral perfection, and the immeasurable, mysterious nature of the Divine that exceeds human grasp.

Themes: divine sovereignty, praise of divine virtues, unfathomable depth of God, divine majesty, recognition of divine greatness, God as treasure of excellence
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The boundless generosity of the Divine as giver and sustainer of all beings overwhelms any human capacity for adequate praise. No mouth, no words, can fully extol the One who provides everything. A confession of creaturely inadequacy before infinite divine bounty, expressing awe rather than despair.

Themes: divine generosity, inadequacy of human praise, awe before the infinite, the Giver and Sustainer, limits of speech, humility in worship
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
Overwhelmed by the boundlessness of the Divine, the speaker asks which virtues could possibly be selected for praise, since they are infinite. The question is itself an act of adoration, declaring the Lord the master and inexhaustible treasury of all excellences, beyond any complete enumeration through singing or speech.

Themes: infinite divine attributes, inadequacy of praise, devotional wonder, God as treasure of virtues, sovereignty of the Divine, limits of human expression
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥: The mind, addressed as a madman, is warned that no one will shelter it even for a moment. The image of being turned away from every house conveys total rejection and homelessness. It admonishes the restless, deluded self that clings to worldly attachments, declaring that such a state earns no refuge anywhere. Themes: admonishing one's own mind, rejection, homelessness, delusion, maya (worldly attachment), urgency, spiritual warning
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
Admonishing the restless mind for its wavering, asking why it doubts when the Divine is the fulfiller of all desires and hopes. The mind's anxiety is met with a reminder of divine sufficiency and providence, urging trust over agitation.

Themes: restless mind, doubt, divine providence, trust, fulfillment of desires, inner stability, surrender
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
Admonishing one's own mind, urging it to join in loving remembrance of the Lord of the Universe. The instruction is direct and personal: the mind, too, must turn to simran (loving remembrance) and dwell on the Divine. It frames meditation not as optional but as the mind's own necessary act of devotion.

Themes: self-admonition, mind, simran, loving remembrance, divine meditation, instruction to the self, devotion
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
The mind is addressed directly and corrected: the treasure it seeks outside already dwells within. The treasure is the Divine itself, the source of all contentment, and the outward search — wandering forests, places, objects — is futile. This is an admonition to one's own mind to turn inward instead of chasing externals.

Themes: inner divinity, treasure within, admonishing the mind, futility of outward search, turning inward, divine indwelling, contentment
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
An admonition addressed to the deluded human mind, calling it insane for being entranced by the visible world of maya (worldly attachment) and losing the true path of life. The speaker demands attention, then confronts the listener with the irrationality of forsaking spiritual purpose for transient sights. It is a wake-up call against worldly distraction.

Themes: delusion, maya, admonishing the mind, spiritual blindness, worldly attachment, call to awareness, losing the path
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
An admonition to one's own restless mind: stop chasing after distractions and instead become the dust beneath the feet of those who have practiced simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine. Dust is the image of utter humility and self-effacement; only by erasing ego and attaching oneself to the devout does union with the Divine become possible.

Themes: humility, self-effacement, surrender, simran, loving remembrance, sangat, company of the devout, ego-dissolution, devotion, refuge
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
The True Guru's single glance of grace outweighs all worldly sovereignty; one merciful look from the Guru confers happiness greater than ruling a hundred thousand kingdoms. The line exalts the Guru's nadar (grace-filled glance) as the supreme gift, declaring that spiritual favour surpasses every earthly pleasure and royal possession.

Themes: Guru's grace, spiritual sovereignty, true happiness, nadar, worthlessness of worldly power, divine glance, contentment beyond kingship
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
The True Guru's grace transforms suffering so completely that pain is no longer experienced as pain. The line declares a state that results from divine mercy: affliction loses its power to afflict. It is a promise about the inner condition of one who has received the Guru's compassionate glance, not a claim that external hardship disappears.

Themes: grace of the True Guru, transcendence of suffering, divine mercy, inner peace, freedom from pain, spiritual protection, equanimity
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The fourth laav (circumambulation of the marriage ceremony) marks the culmination of the soul-bride's union with the Divine: the mind attains sahaj, a state of effortless spiritual equipoise and inner stillness, and the Lord is realised within. The speaker declares this attainment as an offering of loving devotion, expressing gratitude and surrender. The marriage metaphor frames spiritual awakening as the consummation of a sacred bond.

Themes: fourth laav, spiritual marriage, sahaj, inner peace, divine union, realisation of the Lord, surrender, devotion, culmination
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Pleasing the True Guru means making the Guru dwell within the heart; that inward enthronement brings peace and the fruit of every longing. It declares a state of attainment: full contentment and spiritual fulfillment result from heartfelt devotion and surrender, not outward effort.

Themes: peace, contentment, enshrining the Guru in the heart, devotion, surrender, spiritual fulfillment, inner attainment
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
The True Guru is declared an everlasting ally and protector, the one who has cut away the very root and banner of suffering for all who take refuge. The line is a personal testimony of reliance, affirming that the Guru permanently removes the source of pain rather than merely soothing it.

Themes: True Guru as eternal support, refuge and surrender, eradication of suffering at its root, cutting the banner of pain, divine protection, personal testimony of faith
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
The human birth is presented as the singular, appointed opportunity for union with the Divine, the one window in which the soul can meet the Lord of the Universe. It urges recognition that this lifetime is the chance for that meeting, not to be squandered.

Themes: human life as opportunity, urgency of spiritual effort, meeting the Divine, divine union, preciousness of birth, call to awaken
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
Human birth is an opportunity to acquire the true profit: the wealth of the divine Name. The line addresses the mortal directly, reminding him of his purpose in coming into the world — not to accumulate worldly goods but to earn spiritual capital through naam (the divine Name). It frames life as a transaction in which the soul must gain what lasts.

Themes: purpose of human life, earning spiritual profit, naam (divine Name), opportunity of birth, admonishing the mortal, spiritual wealth versus worldly gain
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
Devotional worship of the Divine must be fixed firmly in the heart through meeting the holy. The instruction is direct and urgent: only this steadfast devotion will prove useful in the end. It is a warning against relying on anything else, and an admonition to one's own mind to secure what truly matters.

Themes: firm devotion, meeting the holy, urgent instruction, lasting value, spiritual priority, inner commitment
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
A life is only truly successful when it is spent hearing the divine Name and repeating it in constant remembrance. This is the refrain, declaring the standard by which human existence is judged: not longevity or wealth, but absorption in naam (the divine Name) through listening and simran (loving remembrance). Such a person lives eternally, beyond death.

Themes: fruitful life, hearing the divine Name, chanting and remembrance, immortality through devotion, purpose of human birth, naam, simran
